title: Capacity request intake, SLA windows, and predictive planning for Dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a structured capacity request intake and approval workflow for Dedicated GPU pools that captures throughput requirements, critical SLA windows, and supplies a predictive planner that maps requests to capacity forecasts and staging actions. The outcome should reduce mis-provisioning, shorten approval cycles for standard requests, and surface high-risk requests for manual review.
acceptance_criteria: A single intake form template that captures throughput (peak rps, sustained rps), latency SLOs, burst profiles, regional constraints, and data residency requirements
Automated triage rules that classify requests into Standard / Elevated / Enterprise review lanes within 15 minutes of submission
Approval matrix implemented (automated for Standard requests, 24-hour SLA for Elevated, sales/Legal for Enterprise) documented and linked to playbooks
Predictive planner shows a 12-week capacity forecast after an intake is accepted and proposes autoscaling policy templates and cost delta estimates
Dashboard for intake owners that shows request status, approver timeline, and linked artifacts (PRDs, security reviews, SOC docs)
workflow_steps: Submit intake using new capacity request form (hosted in Confluence/Forms)
Automated triage runs: validate fields, estimate GPU hours, map to region/fleet; tag as Standard/Elevated/Enterprise
For Standard: auto-approve if within mapped headroom; provision via provisioning-runbook and notify customer
For Elevated: route to Capacity Ops lead + Financial owner; 24-hour SLA for approval or escalates to Director
For Enterprise: create a cross-functional approval thread (Security, Legal, Sales) and require onsite constraints and contract clause reviews
After approval: Predictive planner schedules allocations, suggests autoscaling policy (min/max/growth thresholds), and adds capacity reservation to 12-week forecast
Post-provisioning: 2-week health check and 30-day business review with requestor to validate throughput and cost assumptions
stakeholders: Security & Compliance - data residency and audit
open_questions: What threshold for 'standard' headroom should be the default (10% / 20% / 30%)?
Can Finance signoff be automated for requests under $X per month without manual review?
Do we require an explicit security attestation for datasets stored in customer-attached volumes?
How should burst-only workloads be priced vs sustained throughput?
decisions: Use a triage-first model: automated classification to reduce manual approvals
Predictive planner will use 12-week rolling forecast with weekly ingest of historical usage signals
Standard lane auto-approvals limited to requests that fit within existing committed capacity plus 10% buffer
risks: Overly aggressive auto-approval could exhaust buffer and cause production throttles for hosted customers
Inaccurate forecasts for new customers with spiky patterns could cause under-provisioning
Complex approvals for Enterprise customers could slow onboarding and increase sales friction
Insufficient telemetry on early usage could prevent corrective autoscaling policy tuning
